subject: Mermaid Fidelity unsupported verdicts that are Trident's capability assessments (outcome kind `capability-assessment`, unified/mermaid-fidelity/outcome-kinds.ts), checked against the installed candidate artifacts of the 0.4.0 campaign (prepared artifacts: the campaign's community-prepared.json; packages under node_modules/.cache/unified-community/ and node_modules/.cache/fidelity-bridges/).
baseline: The 2026-11-14 jsdom campaign's per-callback results (all 7,346 reference-qualified callbacks per project), classified by unified/mermaid-fidelity/outcome-kinds.ts. baselineCallbacks counts callbacks whose first unsupported reason has that basis.
method: A confirmed assessment is one the installed artifact's own public code agrees with (its detector, validator, renderer or CLI refuses the source, or its public types and exports have no such member), cited by file:line or by a probe result. A disproved one is withdrawn: bound so the candidate's real behaviour is measured, or turned into an adapter limitation (a Trident gap) whose reason names the native evidence. Probes call each project's own public entry on the runtime's example source for the family (runtime.ts `examples`).

assessments.evidence: The test sets `timeline.yy = timelineDB`, where timelineDB is `import * as timelineDB from './timelineDb.js'`: Mermaid's own timeline database module, which Trident already binds to the candidate's model (its getters read the candidate's parse). It is not a caller-supplied database, so no callback protocol is involved.
assessments.action: Bound: runtime.ts treats a family's bound database module set as yy as that family's database (databaseModules), so the candidate's own timeline parse and getters are measured. A reviewed ports timeline view (views/ports.mjs timelineView) reads Pele's and Bezel's periods and Latias94/merman's tasks; without a reviewed view, timeline values pass through only in Mermaid's shapes (upstream-fidelity-projection.mjs), so section records or 'LeftRight' are gaps, not failures.

assessments.scope: xychart.jison.spec.ts and quadrant.jison.spec.ts (a test-supplied mockDB of vi.fn members)
assessments.evidence: Pele 1.13.0's public `pele/diagrams/xychart` and `pele/diagrams/quadrantChart` Diagram objects (package.json exports './diagrams/*') parse by building their own database: dist/esm/chunks/364JUB4J.js `parse(e,t,i){let c=new $t;...;Ue(e,c);return c}`; the database class XyChartDb (dist/diagrams/xychart/db.d.ts) declares setOrientation, setXAxisTitle, setXAxisRangeData, setXAxisBand, setYAxisTitle, setYAxisRangeData, setLineData, setBarData, setDiagramTitle, setAccTitle, setAccDescription, the same callbacks Mermaid's jison grammar makes on yy, and parse() returns that instance. Partial collection with the binding: 74 of the 82 xychart/quadrant callbacks pass and 1 fails natively (Pele rejects `classDef` style `fill`); 7 quadrant callbacks are Pele's own refusal of a mixed-case `QuadRantChart` header ('No diagram type detected for the given text.').
assessments.action: Bound: runtime.ts forwardNativeCalls delivers each outermost call Pele's parser makes on its own database class, with Pele's arguments, to the test's yy (and to a vi.spyOn spy on the test's database). Applies to any candidate whose parse result is an instance of its own database class.

assessments.evidence: bezel-mermaid 0.2.26 crate as the bridge extracts it (node_modules/.cache/fidelity-bridges/crabtalk-bezel/source/bezel-mermaid-0.2.26): src/lib.rs:20 `pub mod diagrams`; src/diagrams/xychart/parser.rs:11 `pub fn parse_xy_chart(src: &str, db: &mut XyChartModel)` and src/diagrams/quadrant/parser.rs:13 `pub fn parse_quadrant(src: &str, db: &mut QuadrantModel)` drive a caller-supplied database through its set_*/add_* methods (src/diagrams/xychart/db.rs:133-224, src/diagrams/quadrant/db.rs:159-198).
assessments.action: Adapter limitation: native-capabilities.mjs records the evidence; once the candidate's own parser accepts the source, the callback is a Trident gap ('implements a xychart parser that drives a caller-supplied database natively ...; Trident does not bind it yet'). A Rust database is a concrete type, so binding it needs a bridge that relays each call; not done here. Native-first parsing now measures the candidate's own rejections: 15 of the 82 pass, 1 fails natively, 1 is Bezel's own refusal, and 65 are adapter limitations.

assessments.evidence: Every other candidate's public parse returns plain data with no database class: bridged models arrive as JSON (bridges.ts protocol), Agentic's editing parser and Frankenmermaid's WASM IR return object literals, and a grep of each installed package (zombie, beautiful, ascii-mermaid, vitepress, opencode merman, crafter, merslim, kitlangton merman, xmermaid, ondine, agentic, frankenmermaid, mermaid_core 0.3.2 lib/, mmdr, mermaid-ascii, termaid, figurehead) finds none of Mermaid's xychart/quadrant/flowchart database member names (setXAxisTitle/set_x_axis_title, addVertex/add_vertex, setDateFormat, setClickEvent). Latias94/merman's diagram modules are crate-private (merman-core 0.10.0 src/lib.rs:58 `mod diagrams`; src/diagrams/mod.rs:47-156 `pub(crate) mod`).
assessments.action: Kept as a capability assessment, but the runtime now asks the candidate's own parser first: a rejection or refusal of the source is measured natively (e.g. 12 xychart callbacks pass for most candidates whose parser rejects the invalid sources the tests expect to throw; candidates without the family record their own refusal, MermaidTUI's 'Unsupported diagram type').

assessments.scope: vi.spyOn on a database member (flow-interactions.spec.js, classDiagram.spec.ts, gantt, sequence, state): 35 callbacks per candidate
assessments.verdict: disproved for the members Pele implements (setClickEvent, setLink on class and flowchart databases); confirmed for the rest
assessments.evidence: Pele's parse result is its database class instance (e.g. dist/diagrams/sequence/db.d.ts SeqDb declares apply, addActor, addMessage, addSignal, addNote; flowchart and class databases declare setLink and setClickEvent). Partial collection with the binding: 31 of Pele's 35 spy callbacks pass; the other 4 (class addRelation, flowchart setDirection, sequence apply, state setRootDoc) inspect Mermaid's own-property layout and stay Trident gaps.
assessments.action: Bound: the runtime offers a spy on a member the candidate's own database class implements (getOwnPropertyDescriptor/defineProperty) and forwardNativeCalls delivers the parser's calls to it; a member the class lacks stays a capability assessment, now checked against the class itself.

assessments.verdict: disproved for the members Bezel implements; confirmed for flowchart setDirection
assessments.evidence: bezel-mermaid 0.2.26 crate as the bridge extracts it (node_modules/.cache/fidelity-bridges/crabtalk-bezel/source/bezel-mermaid-0.2.26): class/db.rs:260 set_click_event, :245 set_link, :124 add_relation; flowchart/store.rs:392 set_link, :405 set_click_event; gantt/db.rs:374 set_click_event, :259 set_today_marker; sequence/db.rs:427 apply; state/db.rs:36 set_root_doc (all `pub fn` in public modules). No set_direction on the flowchart store.
assessments.action: Adapter limitation (native-capabilities.mjs) for the implemented members.

assessments.evidence: No other candidate's public interface has a database the test could spy on: see the jison-callback evidence (plain data models; no Mermaid database member names in the installed packages; Latias94/merman's diagram modules are crate-private).

Natively probed by construction: for Pele the runtime's database is a fresh instance of Pele's own database class (`new Constructor()` from the parse result), and a member is called natively when the class has it (runtime.ts `view[key] ?? raw?.[key]`). The verdict fires only for members the class lacks (treeview addNode, gantt setDisplayMode/parseDuration, usecase createModel, flowchart setDiagramId, getConfig*).

assessments.verdict: disproved for the members listed in unified/mermaid-fidelity/native-capabilities.mjs; confirmed for getConfig, getConfigField, usecase createModel, flowchart makeUniq/exists/setDirection/setDiagramId, agentflow setFrontmatterLineOffset, block edgeStrTo*, requirement setDirection, preserveCommentsWhenParsing
assessments.evidence: bezel-mermaid 0.2.26 crate as the bridge extracts it (node_modules/.cache/fidelity-bridges/crabtalk-bezel/source/bezel-mermaid-0.2.26): each listed member is a `pub fn` on the family's public database type (file:line per member in native-capabilities.mjs), e.g. gantt/db.rs:237 set_date_format, flowchart/store.rs:87 add_vertex, treeview/model.rs:87 add_node, common/outline.rs:113 OutlineDb::add_node (mindmap), er/db.rs:173 add_sub_graph; titles through `pub titles: Titles` (common/db.rs:37-45). A grep of the crate finds no get_config, create_model, make_uniq, exists, set_direction, set_diagram_id or edge_str_to_* function.
assessments.action: Adapter limitation: the runtime reports a test that needs one of these members as a Trident gap naming the evidence ('crabtalk/bezel 0.2.26 implements gantt database setDateFormat natively (...); Trident does not bind it yet'). Binding needs a stateful bridge that calls the crate's database methods; not done here.

assessments.evidence: No Mermaid database API in the public interface: plain-data models (bridged JSON, object literals) and no Mermaid database member names in any installed package (grep, see jison-callback); Latias94/merman's diagram modules are crate-private (merman-core 0.10.0 src/diagrams/mod.rs:47-156 `pub(crate) mod`).

mermaid_core 0.3.2 lib/mermaid_core.dart exports parseC4Diagram, parseClassDiagram, parseErDiagram, parseFlowchart, parseGanttChart, parseJourney, parseMindmap, parsePacket, parsePieChart, parseQuadrantChart, parseRequirementDiagram, parseSankey, parseSequence, parseStateDiagram, parseTimeline, parseXyChart (bridges/dart/build.ts publicCoreParsers). parseRadar, parseGitGraph, parseRailroad, parseArchitecture, parseBlock, parseKanban exist in lib/src/diagrams/* but are not exported, so under SCOPE.md's public-interface rule they are not part of the candidate's parse interface.
assessments.action: Kept (the capability exists only in private code).

assessments.scope: edge ids ("<project>'s edge model keeps no edge ids")
assessments.evidence: node_modules/.cache/unified-community/zombie-mermaid@5.17.0-recipe-*/node_modules/@zombie-mermaid/core/dist/shared/index.d.ts MermaidEdge declares `id?: string` ("Edge id from `A e1@--> B`") and `animate?: boolean` ("Set by `e1@{ animate: true }`"), also in 5.16.0. Probe of `flowchart TD / A --> B / B e2@--> C / e2@{ animate: true }` returns the second edge with id 'e2' and animate true, the first with neither.
assessments.action: View fixed (view-core.mjs mermaidGraphView edgeIds): a written id is Mermaid's user-defined id (isUserDefinedId true) and a written animate is read; an edge written without an id has Mermaid's generated L_<start>_<end>_<n> id declared absent for that edge only. reviewed-versions.mjs 5.17.0 note records the review.

assessments.evidence: Probe of `flowchart TD / A EDGEID@--> B`: no edge carries 'EDGEID' (kitlangton merman reads 'AEDGEID@' as a node id; the others drop it).

assessments.scope: participant and actor recorded the same way
assessments.evidence: Probe of `sequenceDiagram / participant PA / actor AB`: mmdr gives both shape 'ActorBox'; merslim and figurehead keep no kind for either.
Probe of `C4Context / Person(customerA, ...)`: no 'wrap' key in any element record.

Probe of `gitGraph / commit / branch develop / checkout develop / commit / checkout main`: the models keep commits with their branch and the branch list, with no field for the branch checked out last.
